Circle as part of our campaign because almost all students in Saltoro do not ask questions in class, show little interest in their studies, and often lack confidence. The

Circle provides a safe and supportive space where students can share their thoughts, learn to ask questions, build self-confidence, and develop essential life skills, which are the right of every student. In addition, they will learn leadership, decision-making, communication, and negotiation skills, enabling them to actively participate in school and community life. By encouraging open discussion and peer support, the
Circle helps students become active learners, take greater interest in education, and prepare for life beyond school.
is it playing in your campaign strategy
Circle is playing a key role in

in our campaign strategy. By bringing together all girls students in Saltoro, it helps raise awareness about their rights, the importance of education, and the campaign itself. The girls also share this awareness with their parents, creating a stronger community understanding.
Its main purpose is to build their interest in studies and prepare them to actively question and hold teachers accountable. T

hrough peer support and skill-building activities, the Circle organizes girls around shared issues like education participation, leadership, and life skills, strengthening their collective voice and fostering active participation in school and community decisions.
How are you using the circle to move others to act not just attend?

Circle ensures that girls do not just attend sessions but actively participate in the campaign. Through discussions, skill-building activities, and peer support, they develop confidence, leadership, communication, and decision-making skills. Equipped with these skills, girls encourage their peers to engage in school activities, ask questions, and hold teachers accountable. They also share their learning with parents, raising awareness and motivating action across the community. In this way, the Circle transforms passive attendance into active participation, expanding the campaign’s impact beyond the Circle itself.

August, receiving assurances for resolution and support for SMC training.
